key_insight: A two-level framework ranks EHR-derived disease trajectories by semantic novelty and clinical priority, showing that literature-based meaning and reliability can change which motifs are highlighted.
clinical_relevance: This could help researchers focus on more novel, higher-confidence disease trajectories for hypothesis generation, while avoiding overinterpreting structural pattern discovery as clinical significance.
method: Built on 99,527 branching motifs from a patient-disjoint MIMIC-IV pipeline
Embedded three textual variants per motif/node-target pair with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5
Compared motif semantics against 166,972 pre-2023 PubMed references using cosine-distance scoring and reliability-adjusted prioritization
evidence_signal: Across robustness checks, broad ranking was fairly stable, and the high-semantic subgroup showed improved forecasting error (MAE down 20.1 days; sMAPE down 2.37 points), though discrimination gains were inconclusive.
watch_item: The framework measures literature-relative novelty, not causal discovery or clinician-validated novelty, so rankings should not be treated as direct clinical recommendations.
paper_title: A Two-Level Clinical Novelty Prioritization Framework for Disease Trajectories Discovered from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
